releaseNotes: Platform release: Formation now notices when a company's record disagrees with itself in ways that have nothing to do with two claims holding different values for the same key. That older check is a good one, but it can only fire on claims somebody gave a key to, and nothing Formation writes for itself has one — engine results, imported launch work, and generated drafts all arrive without. A workspace could hold a hundred imported claims and still report a perfectly consistent record, because none of them were eligible to be compared.

The new findings are structural, decided by looking at fields rather than at language: a fact with nothing behind it is not a fact; a claim held at 80% or more with no evidence is making a claim about evidence it cannot produce; a deliverable resting on claims that have since been rejected is resting on nothing; a deliverable marked reviewed or approved whose every source is still an assumption says two different things at once; a decision cannot be reviewed before it was made; and work due after the launch it is meant to precede describes a sequence that cannot happen. Nothing is repaired — a contradiction is the founder's to resolve, and two of these have a legitimate answer of "that is fine". Terminology consistency is deliberately not shipped: catching a company that says "families" in one document and "households" in another needs a record of the words that company has chosen, and a matcher without one would flag synonyms as drift and miss the drift that matters. Checks, 174 domain tests, the production build, and the full audit pass.
